> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a9292e6f602bc8acd0483ad99f45c095679e656` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `92917f872349683ce97700976113c4787b3fc6c5` — the merge of head `09243923ba1757cdfa0922b6b358cb5f97e149b9` into base `5a9292e6f602bc8acd0483ad99f45c095679e656`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 92917f872349683ce97700976113c4787b3fc6c5 && git checkout 92917f872349683ce97700976113c4787b3fc6c5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5a9292e6f602bc8acd0483ad99f45c095679e656 09243923ba1757cdfa0922b6b358cb5f97e149b9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5a9292e6f602bc8acd0483ad99f45c095679e656 && git merge --no-ff 09243923ba1757cdfa0922b6b358cb5f97e149b9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a9292e6f602bc8acd0483ad99f45c095679e656
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5a9292e6f602bc8acd0483ad99f45c095679e656` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ea413a0a1486b0fcbef6ec1a194b9fee1b1a8dfa`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21236 (body; comments 5940354474, 5943048346, 5943890476, 5943928162), PR #21282 (body, 11 files, net diff against merge base `ee42f00e`, which is byte-identical to the local three-dot diff), `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.filter-text-operator-declared-type-refused.ts` at `ee42f00e`, tree reads by `git show` / `git grep` at the head and on `origin/main`, and the head's check-runs, read last at 2026-10-02T02:36:35Z.

### ① Derived judgments

**`@objectstack/core` — right.**
- `JsonColumnFieldClass` reaches the package surface through `packages/core/src/index.ts:141` (`export *` from the module), so the diff rightly edits no index. It is a type with no runtime value, and the fourth parameter defaults to `'multi-value-or-json'`; the four callers that pass no class (`objectql/having-filter.ts:1171,1768,1811`, `driver-memory/filter-refusal.ts:909`) keep the former text. Additive public surface and nothing more.
- The `single-value-media` sentence against the landed entry: the entry's acceptance tail reads "A single-value file-class field is not a membership question: it answers text operators again once its deployment finishes the media-column move (the column step of `objectstack migrate files-to-references --apply`)". The PR's `MEDIA_COLUMN_MOVE_REMEDY` says the same with two deliberate substitutions, "text operators" to "these operators" (the door refuses the scalar comparisons too, which the entry covers in its preceding clause) and "its deployment" to "this deployment"; the command string is byte-identical. The reason, "at a single-value file-class field still stored as JSON", matches the entry's "on a SQL deployment still inside the ADR-0104 dual-encoding window (its media columns not yet moved)". Accurate. The arm never names `$contains`: the only `$contains` text lives in `containsRemedy`, which the media arm does not call, and the pin asserts its absence on every refused spelling.
- The default arm is byte-identical by construction: `refusalReason('multi-value-or-json', op)` returns the former string, `refusalRemedy('multi-value-or-json', name)` is `containsRemedy(name)`, and the template keeps the same separators around reason and remedy. The #21067 hash pins (message `f0a54a98…` at 486; diagnostics `da62717a…` 406, `4ff8d528…` 416, `35e2fd3a…` 418) are untouched (the test file's only deletion is its import line), the new control asserts the named class equals the default, and Test Core is green on this head.
- The 500-character cut: `truncateClientMessage` (`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts:82`, `CLIENT_MESSAGE_MAX = 500` at line 45) keeps a message only when its length is strictly less than 500, so "whole" means 499 or fewer. The media message is pinned at 485 (`d76a61be…`); counted from the source constants, the reason loses 12 characters (113 to 101) and the remedy gains 11 (227 to 238) against the 486 default, which gives 485. The media diagnostic names the field once (the subject only; the move remedy carries no name), so the `$startsWith` diagnostic at 408 plus a 91-character name is 499 (whole) and plus 92 is 500 (cut), exactly as the pin asserts. Right.

**`@objectstack/driver-sql` — right.**
- `jsonColumnFieldClass(table, localField)` is `undefined` unless `isJsonColumn` (`:16117`, `jsonFields[table]` membership) and `'single-value-media'` iff `mediaFields[table]` also names the field. The inference is sound: at both registration sites (`:12012-12016` managed, `:12100-12106` external, and the shard copy `:11863/11865`) `mediaCols` takes a field iff `!isMultiValuedColumn && FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES.has(type)` on BOTH arms, and `jsonCols` takes it iff `isJsonField`, whose first branch for exactly that population returns `mediaColumnIsJson()` (`!fileColumnsMoved`, `:19990`) before `JSON_COLUMN_TYPES` is consulted. So the intersection is single-value file-class AND window-at-registration. `initObjects` awaits `resolveFileColumnsMoved()` before `registerObjectMetadata` (`:12265`, then `:12225`), and a `fileColumnsMoved: true` literal is set in the constructor (`:6234`) ahead of any registration, so the window is asked once and frozen into `jsonFields`; this method reads the frozen registry and asks nothing. A field can be in both maps outside the window only through the pre-existing staleness of `jsonFields` itself (a window closed mid-process is read at the next boot), and that same staleness decides whether the gate fires at all, so the class inference is exactly as sound as the gate. Not a second window test, as triage required.
- A `multiple: true` file field is excluded from `mediaFields` by `isMultiValuedColumn`, so it reads `'multi-value-or-json'`; §2 pins it.
- Refused set unchanged: `assertOperatorAppliesToColumn` still returns on an operator outside `JSON_COLUMN_INCOMPATIBLE_OPERATORS` and now on `jsonColumnFieldClass === undefined`, which is precisely `!isJsonColumn`; `code` and `status` come from the unchanged `withheldFilterError`. `jsonColumnOperatorError` has one call site (`:16423`), updated. `SqliteWasmDriver extends SqlDriver` with no override of the gate and inherits correctly. `Clause-②: no` is right.

**`@objectstack/driver-turso` — right, and the amendment-recorded face was the correct call.**
- `JsonColumnResolver` now answers the class; `RemoteTransport.isJsonColumn` is re-expressed as `jsonColumnFieldClass(...) !== undefined` and its remaining caller (the membership predicate, `:3592`) keeps its meaning because `TursoDriver` maps the former `true` to a class and `false` to `undefined`. All three refusal sites (`:3162`, `:3434`, `:3459`) pass the class; the seam test's resolver is updated to the class shape.
- "A JSON column on every remote deployment" is exact: `toKnexConfig` forwards no `fileColumnsMoved` (`:649`, and the builder at `:1949/1956` carries none), `setFileColumnsMovedResolver` returns `false` without installing on the remote face (`:4040-4043`), only `SqlDriver.initObjects` asks the resolver and no remote schema door reaches it, and `planMediaColumnMove` refuses with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / 501 (`:3661`, `refuseRemoteMediaColumnMove` `:665`). So `fileColumnsMoved` stays false for the process's life there, every single-value file-class field registers into both maps, and the remote face reads `'single-value-media'`. Leaving it on a boolean would have had one `TursoDriver` print two sentences for one filter; the parity pin holds local and remote to one answer across 16 cases.
- Is the new remedy misleading on the remote face? The remedy is a conditional whose antecedent that transport cannot yet satisfy; the command it names refuses loudly, with the reason and with "keeps these columns on the JSON encoding" in its own sentence. The author is steered to an explained 501, not to an operator that silently answers no rows. Not false; incomplete on that one face. Judged under ③.

**Per-face conclusions — right.** `declaredJsonStoredFields` is at `having-filter.ts:966-976` and is `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES.has(type) || isMultiValueField(...)`; `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` is json, composite, repeater, record, location, address, vector, no file class, so the engine's per-aggregation `filter` never meets the second class and the default is right. `isJsonStoredField` is at `memory-driver.ts:2391-2395` with the same predicate and a docblock that excludes single-value media by design. No other producer of the builder exists at the head (core, objectql x3, driver-memory x1, driver-sql x1, driver-turso remote x1), so the face table is complete.

**Pins and the reported ablation — they prove what they claim.**
- driver-sql pin: 16 cases (1 population, §1 five per-type plus the `$contains` no-rows and presence cases, §2 two, §3 five plus the control). Refusals are asserted by `code`/`status` and by EQUALITY with the builder for the class, never by literal words, so the builder's hash pins and this pin cannot drift apart. A mutation making `jsonColumnFieldClass` answer `'multi-value-or-json'` for media while keeping the `undefined` guard reddens exactly the five §1 per-type cases and nothing else (the `$contains` and presence cases are data answers, §2 expects the default words, §3 is `undefined` on either arm): "5 red / 11 green" is the shape the file predicts.
- Turso parity pin: 16 cases (2 fields by 5 operators plus bare plus null = 14, the no-`$contains` case, the control); the mutation reddens 14 plus 1 and spares the control: "15 red / 1 green" matches.
- Core: 14 `it` plus a 3-row `it.each` is the 17 reported. The multi-valued `$contains` refusal is pinned byte-for-byte as the control on both drivers and both faces, and `$contains` answers membership (`r1`) beside it, so the control discriminates.
- Cross-package reverse check: handing the resolver `this.isJsonColumn(object, field)` is `boolean` against `JsonColumnFieldClass | undefined`, a TS2322 at `turso-driver.ts:1818` (the expression line of the arrow at `:1817-1819`). Right direction, not re-run here.
- Cited base line numbers hold at `ee42f00e`: builder `:229`, `containsRemedy` `:174`, `mediaColumnIsJson` `:19944`, `isJsonField` `:19969`.

### ② Semver level

Three `patch` changesets (`@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, all at 17.5.0), each with `Clause-②: no` at line start, and the PR body carries it at line 3. The refused operators, the refused fields and the `code`/`status` do not move; only the sentence for one class of column does, so `Clause-②: no` is accurate, and under the Post-Task rule (a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`; only `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`) `patch` is right for the additive type plus the defaulted parameter. The three bodies are accurate against the code, including the turso body's "the remote transport refuses to plan the column step (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / 501), as before".

One place a stricter reading wants `minor`, named and escalated, not blocking: `RemoteTransport` is a published export (`driver-turso/src/index.ts:38`) and `setJsonColumnResolver`'s parameter type is REPLACED, so a host's boolean-returning resolver no longer compiles. The setter's own precedent, #21178, shipped `minor`, but on `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; its ADR-0087 marker treats "a published type narrowed" as its own category, and no gate measures it here (`packages/spec/api-surface` is the only baseline). The only producer is in-tree, `JsonColumnResolver` is not re-exported by name, and the changeset carries the FROM-to-TO mapping the house asks of a breaking entry. Patch stands by the letter of the rule; the seat decides whether the house vocabulary counts a type-surface replacement on a delegate seam.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation 1, the `driver-turso` face: recorded by amendment 5943928162 and judged under ① as the right change (same defect class, same gate family, parity pinned). Accepted; the seat has already restated the stop-first rule for the next card.
- Deviation 2, `origin/main` not merged: `main` has moved 11 commits since `ee42f00e` (to `4e6dc2338a`). The only overlapping file is `sql-driver.ts`; `main`'s three hunks (#21259: the `undeclaredAuditTimestampFields` declaration `:5498`, `registerManagedObjectMetadata` `:12068`, `formatInput` `:20047`) and the PR's four (import `:161`, `jsonColumnOperatorError` `:3404-3419`, `jsonColumnFieldClass` `:16122-16145`, `assertOperatorAppliesToColumn` `:16419-16423`) are disjoint by line, by function and by registry, with no shared symbol. `mergeable_state` is `clean`. The queue rebuild is safe. The §10 "pull `main` before opening a PR" step was skipped; that is a process deviation, and the queue's CI on the merged tree is the backstop. The `check:doc-authoring` red the dev saw against `main`'s newer prose-id baseline sits in a file `main` rewrote together with that baseline, so it resolves in the merge.
- Deviation 3, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally: `ci.yml:2150` runs it inside `Build Core`, a required context that is green on this head. Closed by the gate.
- Deviations 4 to 6: the conformance "before" from a throwaway worktree at BASE is a reporting detail (both readings exit 0, same count); the rest-pin prerequisite was a build-order fact, not a measurement, and the rerun was green; the commit trailers on all four commits are the model-free pair AGENTS.md line 453-454 prescribes, which the harness reminder's model-named form would have had the pre-push hook refuse. Deviation 6 is not a deviation; it is conformance.
- Open question A / B / C: A is right for this PR. The shared sentence keeps one text per column class in a builder that "never reads a declaration"; B would add a transport branch to it and give one driver two sentences; C is a capability expansion with no named remote user. On the remote face the sentence points at a command that refuses with its reason, which is the pre-existing gap, not this PR's. No decision blocks.
- Out-of-scope finding, the remote media-column move gap: noted by the dev, not filed, carrier none. Escalated to the seat: now that the refusal names a command that answers 501 on that transport, the gap wants either a card in the engine lane (remote planner and resolver, option C, on a named remote user) or an explicit no-card ruling. Not blocking.

**Check-runs on the head** (read last, 2026-10-02T02:36:35Z): 34 runs, 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in): conditional jobs), 0 failures, 0 in progress. All seven required contexts of the `main` ruleset are `success`: TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard. Check Changeset `success`; legacy status Vercel `success`. No required job is still running, so the gate verdict is complete.
